data.title: Irruptive Metals Raises Pimentón Interest to 61%, Securing Majority Control
data.description:
The latest update is out from Irruptive Metals Corp. ( (TSE:IRR) ).

Irruptive Metals is a Canadian copper-gold exploration company focused on high-quality projects in Chile, including its flagship Pimentón copper-gold project. Its wholly owned Chilean subsidiary amended its option agreement with Minera Tamidak, increasing the company’s interest in Pimentón from 17% to 61% through a C$3.5 million payment.

The amendment gives Irruptive majority ownership and control approximately five years earlier than originally contemplated, while reducing total payments to Tamidak from C$32.5 million to C$30.5 million. With its 61% interest, the company is entitled to appoint two of three joint-venture directors, including the chair, and the existing 2.5% gross sales royalty arrangements remain unchanged.

data.title: Artemis Drills Through Nullarbor Cover Into Sharon Dam Basement
data.description:
Artemis Resources ( (AU:ARV) ) has shared an announcement.

Artemis Resources’ maiden diamond hole at Sharon Dam has passed through the Nullarbor cover sequence and intersected interpreted Proterozoic basement at 343.3 metres below surface. Drilling was continuing in the basement at a current depth of approximately 348.8 metres.

Sharon Dam is the Madura Province’s strongest known combined magnetic and gravity anomaly, with a modelled source beginning about 400 metres below surface and extending more than 4 kilometres along strike. The target remains conceptual: its cause is unknown, and there is no certainty drilling will intersect mineralisation.

data.title: Soma Gold Reports Q3 2026 Financial Results
data.description:
Soma Gold ( (TSE:SOMA) ) just unveiled an announcement.

Soma Gold, a mining company focused on gold production and exploration in Antioquia, Colombia, reported Q3 2026 revenue of $23.8 million, up 31% from $18.1 million a year earlier; YTD revenue fell 3% to $66.7 million from $69.0 million. Income from mine operations dropped to $3.0 million from $5.3 million, and gross margin narrowed to 13% from 29%.

Adjusted EBITDA fell to $3.0 million in Q3 and $9.8 million year to date, from $6.9 million and $28.9 million, respectively. The company posted a Q3 net loss of $2.4 million, versus net income of $0.4 million, while its YTD net loss was $8.4 million versus income of $5.2 million.

Management attributed the lower margin to higher production costs as mined and milled tonnage increased to offset lower-than-expected grades at Cordero; the average realized cash margin fell to US$1,102 per ounce from US$1,676. Mill throughput rose 39% year over year, while gold grade declined to 3.98 grams per tonne from 5.75 grams per tonne, and production was 4,224 AuEq ounces versus a 7,605-ounce budget.

At September 30, Soma had $8.9 million of working capital and $0.4 million in cash, down from $17.2 million and $6.3 million at year-end 2025. Value-added tax receivables rose to $19.8 million from $12.4 million.

data.title: TruScreen announces a change to June 30 reporting
data.description:
TruScreen Group Ltd. ( (NZ:TRU) ) has issued an update.

TruScreen Group is a medical device company focused on AI-enabled cervical-cancer screening, with a business concentrated in Asia and a growing distribution network in Africa. The company announced a change in its reporting date from March 31 to June 30 to align reporting with seasonal distributor activity and its Australian operations.
